Chicago Progressive Ideology Map

Understanding the Ideology Score

This map shows progressive ideology scores for each Chicago precinct, controlling for racial demographics and urbanist factors (renter %, transit use).

What the Colors Mean:

  • ■ Pink = More progressive than the city as a whole (positive score)
  • ■ Gray = Votes like citywide average (score ≈ 0)
  • ■ Green = More conservative than the city as a whole (negative score)

How to Read the Score:

  • Score = 0: Precinct votes exactly like the citywide average
  • Score = +10: Precinct gives progressives ~10 points more than citywide
  • Score = -10: Precinct gives progressives ~10 points less than citywide

Key Insight: This ideology score is what remains AFTER we account for race, renter status, and transit use. It represents the "true" progressive vs. conservative lean independent of demographics.

Limitations: This is supposed to only be applied to mayoral races because that is all this is taking into account. 2019 was too messy in the first round and Lori dominated too much in the second round to have any insights. The population has moved around and the electorate has probably changed since 2015 though so some areas might be a little off. In particular I think downtown could be skewing too conservative and places near O'Hare and Mount Greenwood might not be showing up as conservative enough.It is also relative to the city. In any given political environment progressives could have factors that boost them or hurt them.

Model Details:

Range: -25.6 to 27.1
Mean: 0.00
Based on: 2015 and 2023 elections normalized to 50/50 split between the more and less progressive candidate. Garcia and Johnson were used as the progressive candidates
